figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1 | Development of engineering strategies applied to construct lutein-
producing strain. a, MEP pathway flux enforcement via the overexpression 
of the crtE gene and deletion of the crtEb and crtYe/f genes. b, Glucose uptake 
system engineering via the overexpression of the iolT1, iolT2 and ppgk genes. 
c, Haem pathway flux enforcement via the deletion of the hmuO gene and the 
overexpression of the hemL, hemAfbr and dtxR genes. d, Metabolic pathways 
for the biosynthesis of lutein from glucose. e, P450 reductase engineering via 
the truncation of N-terminal regions of the ATR2 enzyme in various lengths. 
f, Construction of the electron-channelling scaffold via the fusion of scaffold 
formation tags (RIDD/RIAD) to cytochrome P450 enzymes (trLUT5 and trLUT1) 
and their reductase partner enzyme (trATR2v3). The OH bonds on the β-ring and 
ε-rings are marked in red to indicate the hydroxylation reaction mediated by

Fig. 4 | Optimization of electron-channelling scaffold construct for improved 
lutein production. a, A schematic illustration of the construction of the electron-
channelling scaffold comprising the trATR2v3, trLUT5 and trLUT1 enzymes, 
which are required to convert α-carotene to lutein. The specific interactions of 
RIAD and RIDD peptides that are fused to the C-terminal region of each enzyme 
enabled the recruitment of the peptide tag-fused enzymes in scaffold forms.
